answer: Each identity claims a karst reach, locks a 70-credit bond, and buys a discharge permit. It files one sample per epoch; the gauge logs its sediment plume, and an auditor recomputes load from the public flow table, burning over-limit bonds. Permit price follows sequence, not wallet: first 33, kth 33+6(k-1), 1000th 6027, so 1,000 fakes pay 3,030,000 plus 70,000 bonds. A dilution ring fails: sample keys bind to filing key and hour, and the nadir gauge log never matches a reused sample, so both bonds burn. An honest operator pays 33 once, recovering its bond after a clean epoch.
